content:
Apple's new generation M6 chip made its debut last week in the new Mac mini, but several more products will be upgraded to M6 in the near term. Below is the rumored release timeline for M6 Macs and M6 iPad Pro.

This autumn: M6 MacBook Pro, M6 iMac

Rumors suggest Apple will launch two new M6 Macs this autumn (likely in October or early November):

  • MacBook Pro
  • iMac

The MacBook Pro will only be the 14-inch base model. According to Mark Gurman, Apple will skip the M6 Pro and Max versions, so only the entry-level MacBook Pro will feature the M6, and the next batch of Pro-tier chips will be the M7 Pro and M7 Max in 2027.

Apple's new iMac is not expected to change much beyond the upgrade to the M6 chip, with the only other rumored upgrade being a few new colour options. However, jumping from M4 to M6 should be enough to make this new machine worth the upgrade.

It is worth noting that the rumoured touchscreen MacBook Pro/Ultra is not on this list. Although it is expected to launch soon, it will use the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips rather than the M6.

Early 2027: M6 MacBook Air, M6 iPad Pro

After this autumn, the next batch of products rumoured to be upgraded to the M6 includes:

  • MacBook Air
  • iPad Pro

The new M6 MacBook Air is expected to launch in early 2027, possibly anytime between February and April, but based on Apple's usual pattern, March is a safer bet.

Beyond the chip upgrade, there aren't many rumours about the new MacBook Air, and it is expected to retain the same design as the M5 model. Reports suggest the OLED upgrade won't come until 2028 at the earliest, so the display should remain unchanged.

Apple last updated the iPad Pro in autumn 2025, when it was equipped with the M5 chip. Rumours suggest there will be a new round of updates in spring 2027, meaning this product will follow its usual 18-month upgrade cycle.

Beyond the upgrade to the M6 chip, Apple's new iPad Pro is expected to feature a vapour chamber cooling design, which should improve the sustained performance of this ultra-thin device.

For both the MacBook Air and iPad Pro, one potential benefit of the M6 is improved battery life. Apple says the M6's 2-nanometre process brings "major leaps in performance and energy efficiency".

Are you planning to upgrade to any of these M6 products? Why? Feel free to let us know in the comments section.
